summary: Checkpoint call with DeltaWare on renewal timing and a proposed capacity uplift including an EU region add-on. Main open items: final pricing (commit vs burst), SOC2/KMS details for procurement, pilot benchmarking plan for latency in EU, and contract amendment timeline. AE/SE aligned on next steps to deliver pricing and run a short pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Noah (Redwood SE), Jorge (Redwood CSM); Asha (Head ML Ops), Tom (CTO), Lina (Procurement)
Links shared: pricing deck (link), eu-benchmark-sheet.xlsx (link), security-summary.pdf (link)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate you making time, quick agenda — renewal timing, capacity uplift numbers, and the eu region add-on, and then we'll close with next steps.
[00:18] Asha: thanks, Samira. we just want to make sure the numbers line up with our holiday traffic spike and the eu residency requirements.
[00:30] Noah: quick note — i can run a targeted benchmark from our eu edge nodes to mirror your traffic pattern, i just need a representative route breakdown.
[00:45] Tom: yeah, and we want to confirm latency SLOs if we add the eu region; also interested in private vpc option for a subset of sensitive requests.
[01:05] Jorge: procurement side, hi, Lina. what's the runway for contract signoff? any process constraints?
[01:18] Lina: hi — we've got Q1 budget approvals but procurement needs SOC2 evidence and a short summary of KMS/HSM integration; plus any data residency guarantees in the amendment.
[01:36] Samira: totally, we can share our SOC2 + iso documents and a short KMS integration note. on residency we offer eu-hosted model endpoints and an on-prem/private option for regulated flows.
[01:52] Asha: can you give the tradeoffs — if we go hosted eu vs private vpc for just user PII flows? like cost and latency tradeoffs.
[02:08] Noah: sure — hosted eu endpoint: lowest time-to-value, reasonable latencies (15-40ms token for most models, depending on sequence length), lower ops overhead. private vpc: better isolation and control, small added latency (depends on customer network egress), and higher fixed monthly cost because of dedicated capacity. plus we can do a hybrid — pin sensitive routes to vpc, everything else on hosted.
[02:35] Tom: what's 'higher fixed monthly' look like? percentwise?
[02:42] Samira: typically 20-40% uplift relative to hosted unit costs for the reserved capacity model; if you commit it's cheaper per token, burst rates are more expensive but give elasticity.
[02:58] Asha: for the holiday spike we need 30% headroom for peak, so we're exploring committed + burst mix.
[03:08] Noah: we can size committed pools to handle baseline plus automatica burst to cover peaks — automatic burst is charged at a premium. i'll sketch a sample sizing in the benchmark doc.
[03:25] Lina: procurement will want the draft amendment that lists eu as an active region and the data handling clause.
[03:33] Samira: yes, we'll draft an amendment during the renewal; timeline? we were thinking sign by end of december to lock pricing before january.
[03:42] Tom: end of december is good if we get the numbers this week.
[04:00] -- topic: pricing and discounting --
[04:10] Samira: proposed options: A) 12-month renewal with 30% capacity uplift (committed) + 6 months of burst buffer; B) 24-month with 40% uplift and deeper per-token discounts; C) smaller 6-month pilot for eu + then commit.
[04:32] Asha: option A seems reasonable, but we want optionality to expand after pilot. can you articulate the price breakpoints?
[04:44] Samira: i'll put tiered pricing in the slide deck; baseline committed per-token, burst surcharge, and an eu-region premium.
[04:52] Jorge: i can share last quarter's usage shape which will inform tier thresholds — action item for me.
[05:05] -- 05:05 to 07:00 roughly technical deep dive --
[05:10] Noah: on the tech side, two items: kv cache behaviour across regions, and model variants. there are some gotchas if you have long-context sessions — cross-region kv cache misses can increase token counts.
[05:30] Asha: we have a lot of multi-turn flows with longer context, so kv cache is important. any recommendations?
[05:38] Noah: recommend session stickiness to eu endpoints for eu users to avoid cross-region cache misses; also quantization profile tuning for throughput.
[05:48] Tom: are model variants auto-fallback compatible? like if eu capacity is full, can requests route to us-east?
[05:56] Samira: yes, smart routing can fallback to other compatible model variants — we can make a policy that keeps PII flows in-region and fail open to non-PII routes.
[06:10] Asha: okay good.
[06:22] -- timestamp jump, procurement specifics --
[06:25] Lina: for the amendment we need: exact capacity numbers, eu region as a mapped geography, a statement on logs retention and encryption in transit + at rest, and SSO / SAML integration note.
[06:40] Samira: understood. we'll include SSO/SAML details and retention defaults; we also support customer-managed KMS for private deployments.
[06:50] Lina: does redwood support bring-your-own-key for hosted eu? (transcription: "does redwood support bring-your-own-key for hosted e u?" -> may be misheard)
[07:00] Noah: for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for enterprise tiers; for private VPC it's straightforward to bring HSM/KMS.
[07:12] Tom: any compliance red flags for us? we are in finance and need audit trails.
[07:20] Jorge: we log request-level metadata and have audit log exports; i'll attach a sample export format.
[07:28] -- timestamp: 07:28 --
[07:30] Asha: about benchmarking — we want to run a 2-hour window that simulates peak traffic and measures p95 latency and token cost. can you run that from an eu vantage point?
[07:41] Noah: yes. i'll configure the harness and need two example routes plus expected concurrency and sequence length distribution.
[07:52] Asha: i'll send those by end of day tomorrow.
[08:05] Samira: perfect. we'll queue the benchmark and aim to run by week of 2025-12-15.
[08:15] -- mid call discussion on competitors and procurement levers --
[08:20] Tom: we've seen comparable numbers from ManagedCloudX and Anthropic; pricing and support SLAs are key.
[08:30] Samira: understood — we can show committed discount ladders and an SLA addendum for dedicated pools.
[08:42] Lina: are there setup fees or one-time provisioning costs for private vpc?
[08:48] Samira: there can be a one-time onboarding fee for private on-prem or VPC setups — i'll include an estimate in the pricing table.
[08:58] -- later, edge case discussion --
[09:10] Noah: small note on KV: if you have cross-region users, consider geolocation routing to minimize cache thrashing. also model checkpoint serialization needs slight tuning when quantized models run across variants.
[09:36] Asha: ok makes sense.
[09:44] -- wrap up section --
[09:50] Samira: to recap: we will send an updated pricing deck that includes eu region premium, committed + burst options, and setup fees. Noah will run the eu benchmark once Asha supplies routes. Jorge will provide usage shape. we'll draft an amendment that adds eu region and +30% capacity.
[10:12] Tom: timeline looks good — please get the docs this week so procurement can review.
[10:20] Lina: yes, procurement needs security summary and the amendment draft to start redlining.
[10:28] Samira: we'll deliver those. any final questions?
[10:34] Asha: one more — if we need to shorten commitment after the pilot, is there a mid-term adjustment clause?
[10:42] Samira: we can add a flexibility clause for re-evaluations at 90 days post-go-live; i'll propose wording.
[10:50] Tom: that's helpful.
[11:00] -- meeting closes --
[11:05] Samira: thanks everyone. next steps as discussed.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KMS -> K M S, KV cache -> K V cash), some speaker labels consolidated. Natural pauses and cross talk were present.
